To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the BMP-2 mRNA is present in the oocytes and early embryos, 2) BMP-2 mRNA and protein is present in the dorsal blastomeres and the animal cap, 3) BMP-2 is expressed in the neural crest, 4) BMP-2 overexpressed in the dorsal blastmores leads to ventral mesodermal differentiation, and 5) BMP-2 can override the dorsalizing activity in animal cap explants.

BMP-2 is transcribed in oocytes and early cleavage stages, and that BMP-2 transcripts become localized to neural crest, pineal body, olfactory placode and heart anlage during gastrulation and neurulation, respectively.
the BMP-2 transcription pattern in Xenopus laeis is very similar to the one described in other species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying the formation of the vertebrate body plan.
the role of BMP-2 in the development of Xenopus.
the role of BMP-2 in early development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

BMP-2, as well as BMP-4, are involved in the formation of ventral mesodermal structures, but that the BMP-2 transcripts, in contrast to those of the BMP-4 gene (and BMP-7, -6, -5), are also present in early cleavage stage Xenopus embryos.
the BMP-2 and BMP-4 genes play an important role in the early development in the formation of the neural crest and the heart anlage.
the BMP family members are involved in a number of developmental processes, including the formation of the dorsal lip, the neural tube and the neural crest.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BMP-2 is involved in early mesoderm induction and in neural crest formation, and that it is involved in the development of the olfactory placodes.

the BMP family members BMP-2 and BMP-4 are involved in the specification of mesodermal cell fates, and that the BMP family genes are expressed in a spatial and temporal pattern which suggests a role for these factors in the formation of mesoderm and in the induction of neural crest cells and the heart anlage.
BMP-2 and BMP-4 are functionally redundant in the early development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BMP-2 and BMP-4 have similar roles in Xenopus development.
BMP-2 is a key regulator in early development of Xenopu laevis and it may play a role in the formation of ventral mesodermal tissues.
BMP-2 is a very important protein in the development of the embryo.
